summary.title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
summary.subtitle: Whole-chapter recap — from cutting DNA to a purified, quality-tested product.
summary.definition: Biotechnology uses living organisms, cells, enzymes or molecular components to make useful products and services. Its two core techniques are genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering.

panels.heading: Recombinant DNA technology
points: Genetic engineering alters DNA or RNA and transfers selected material into a host to change its phenotype.
Bioprocess engineering maintains sterile conditions for large-scale growth of a desired microbe or cell.
In 1972 Cohen and Boyer linked an antibiotic-resistance gene with a Salmonella typhimurium plasmid.
Three basic steps: identify desirable DNA, introduce it into a host, then maintain and transmit it to progeny.

panels.heading: Restriction enzymes
points: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA; endonucleases cut at positions within DNA.
Hind II was the first sequence-specific restriction endonuclease described.
EcoRI is named from Escherichia coli strain RY13; the Roman numeral gives the order of isolation.
A DNA palindrome reads the same on both strands in the 5-prime to 3-prime direction, such as GAATTC paired with CTTAAG.
Staggered cutting leaves complementary single-stranded sticky ends that help DNA ligase act.

panels.heading: Cloning vectors
points: The origin of replication (ori) starts replication and controls the copy number of the linked DNA.
A selectable marker such as antibiotic resistance lets transformants grow while non-transformants are eliminated.
A vector should carry very few, preferably one, recognition site for a given restriction enzyme.
pBR322 is an E. coli vector carrying ori, ampR, tetR and several restriction sites.
A disarmed Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens delivers genes to plants; disarmed retroviruses deliver them to animal cells.

panels.heading: Selecting recombinants
points: Insertion at the BamHI site in tetR disrupts tetracycline resistance while ampicillin resistance remains.
Insertion within the beta-galactosidase coding sequence prevents blue colour on a chromogenic substrate.
Non-recombinants with active beta-galactosidase form blue colonies; recombinants form colourless or white colonies.
A transformant has taken up vector DNA; only some transformants also carry the foreign insert.

panels.heading: Getting DNA into a host
points: DNA is hydrophilic and does not cross the cell membrane easily, so hosts must be made competent.
Divalent calcium ions increase bacterial competence to take up DNA.
Heat shock: incubate cells with recombinant DNA on ice, hold briefly at 42 degrees C, then return to ice.
Microinjection delivers DNA into an animal cell nucleus; biolistics shoots DNA-coated gold or tungsten particles into plant cells.

panels.heading: Amplification and separation
points: PCR repeats denaturation, primer annealing and extension to amplify a selected DNA segment.
Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus stays active through repeated high-temperature denaturation.
Agarose gel electrophoresis separates fragments by size; smaller fragments travel farther.
DNA is negatively charged and migrates toward the anode, the positive electrode.
Ethidium bromide staining under UV light reveals bright orange DNA bands, which are then eluted.

panels.heading: Expression and downstream processing
points: A protein expressed in a heterologous host is called a recombinant protein.
A bioreactor supplies optimum temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins and oxygen.
A stirred-tank bioreactor is a cylindrical vessel with a curved base, a stirrer and a sparger.
Downstream processing separates, purifies, formulates and preserves the product.
Products, especially drugs, undergo strict quality control before marketing.

steps.label: Isolation of DNA
steps.detail: Lysozyme, cellulase or chitinase break the cell wall; ribonuclease and protease remove RNA and protein.

steps.label: Precipitation
steps.detail: Purified DNA precipitates in chilled ethanol as visible fine threads.

steps.label: Cutting of DNA
steps.detail: The same restriction enzyme cuts source DNA and vector so their sticky ends are compatible.

steps.label: Separation and elution
steps.detail: Agarose gel separates fragments by size; the required band is cut out and the DNA extracted.

steps.label: Amplification by PCR
steps.detail: Denaturation, annealing and extension repeat to produce an enormous number of copies of the target.

steps.label: Ligation
steps.detail: DNA ligase seals the sugar-phosphate backbones to make a stable recombinant molecule.

steps.label: Transformation
steps.detail: Competent cells, microinjection, biolistics or disarmed vectors carry recombinant DNA into the host.

steps.label: Selection
steps.detail: Selectable markers and insertional inactivation identify the cells that carry the insert.

steps.label: Expression in a bioreactor
steps.detail: Host cells grow under controlled conditions and express the cloned gene as a recombinant protein.

steps.label: Downstream processing
steps.detail: The product is separated, purified, formulated and quality tested before release.

terms.meaning: DNA made by joining fragments from two different sources.
DNA molecule that carries foreign DNA into a host and replicates there.
Sequence where replication begins; it also controls the copy number of the linked DNA.
Gene that identifies transformants and allows only them to grow under selective conditions.
Loss of a gene's function because foreign DNA has been inserted inside its coding sequence.
Cell that has taken up vector DNA, whether or not it carries the foreign insert.
Complementary single-stranded overhangs left by a staggered restriction cut.
Cell treated, usually with divalent calcium ions, so that it can take up DNA.
Vessel that grows cells at scale under controlled conditions to make a desired product.
Recovery, purification, formulation and quality testing carried out after biosynthesis.

remember: Restriction in restriction enzyme means cutting DNA only at a specific recognition site.
Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA; endonucleases cut within it.
DNA moves toward the anode, the positive electrode, because it is negatively charged.
Ethidium bromide staining makes DNA visible under UV light, not in visible light.
Cutting comes before ligation: source DNA and vector must be cut first, then joined.
Cloning here means making many identical copies of a DNA fragment, not producing a whole animal.
Transformant and recombinant are not synonyms; only some transformants carry the insert.
Downstream processing begins after the product has been synthesised, not during cloning.
